subtopics.name: Government Intervention to Address Market Failure

parts.problem_md:
A government approved the construction of a new railway line connecting major cities. It would be built by a private company but be funded partly through taxation. It would create many jobs. People living on the route worried about the harm to their environment.

Which concepts are directly involved in this statement?
parts.solution_md:
**D is correct** as there are many private benefits (jobs and funding) as well as the external cost to the environment

- A is incorrect as it does not include either of these
- B is incorrect as there is no indication of perfect competition amongst firms
- C is incorrect as there is no government intervention in a market system

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the demand curve D<sub>1</sub> and supply curve S<sub>1</sub> for a good. The government introduces a subsidy to encourage production.

![june-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q18](assets/001-june-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q18.png)

What will be the total cost of the subsidy to the government?
parts.solution_md:
**B is correct** as the cost of the subsidy = (\$30 - \$20) x 5 = \$50

- A is incorrect as the calculation incorrectly uses the old equilibrium quantity (4)
- C is incorrect as the answer is derived by incorrectly multiplying the new equilibrium price and quantity
- D is incorrect as it takes the higher value (\$30) generated by the subsidy and multiplies it by the equilibrium quantity - which does not represent the cost of the subsidy to the government

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the effect of the imposition of a tax on a product.

![qp-june-2019v2-paper-1-cie-economics-igcse-q17](assets/002-qp-june-2019v2-paper-1-cie-economics-igcse-q17.png)

Which area represents the part of the tax paid by consumers of the product?
parts.solution_md:
**A is correct **as areas U + V represent the consumer portion of the tax while areas X and Y represent the producer portion of the tax paid

- B is incorrect as W is part of the welfare loss caused by the tax and does not represent tax paid
- C is incorrect as UVXY represent the total tax burden - not just the consumer share
- D is incorrect as X is part of the producer burden of the tax

parts.problem_md: A private sector firm is given a contract by the government to supply a country’s water. Which government directive will minimise the risk of market failure?
parts.solution_md:
**B is correct **as by ensuring the firm supplies everyone, market failure is prevented

- A is incorrect as this would be market failure
- C is incorrect as maximising profits and using high prices to do so would prevent some households from gaining access to water - a market failure
- D is incorrect as only providing water to those who can pay for it would prevent some households from gaining access to water - a market failure

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: allow the firm to ration water rather than meet demand

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: ensure the firm’s supply includes all areas which are expensive to service

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: insist that the firm aims to maximise profits

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: instruct the firm to provide water only to those who can pay for it

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the impact of a government imposing an indirect tax on a good. The original demand curve is D<sub>1</sub> and original supply curve is S<sub>1</sub>.

![nov-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q19](assets/003-nov-2019-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q19.png)

What is the total tax revenue gained by the government?
parts.solution_md:
**A is correct** as the tax revenue is calculated as (\$60-\$40) x 80 units = \$1,600

- B is incorrect as this multiplies the new equilibrium quantity by the price producers will actually receive for their product (\$40)
- C is incorrect as as this just multiplies the new equilibrium price by the new quantity
- D is incorrect this multiplies the old equilibrium quantity by the old equilibrium price

**C is correct** as the existence of external benefits indicates more of the good/service should be provided than is currently provided

- A is incorrect as government provision of services is a method used to correct market failure
- B is incorrect there is no market failure when social costs = private costs (no external costs)
- D is incorrect as perfect competition is desired in order to avoid market failures such as monopolies and high prices

parts.problem_md:
A major highway has been built at a cost of US\$175 million between Nairobi, Kenya and its suburbs. This reduces travel time and increases safety, but there are environmental problems for small enterprises along its route.

Who bears the external costs of this project?
parts.solution_md:
**D is correct** as the external cost is carried by small enterprises along the route (in the form of CO2 and noise pollution)

- A is incorrect as the authorities bear the private costs not the external costs
- B is incorrect as the cost of travel is a private cost for the passengers when using the service
- C is incorrect as the companies who built the highway received the private benefit (revenue from construction)

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: the authorities who paid for the highway

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: the commuters who travel to work in Nairobi

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: the construction companies that built the highway

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: the small enterprises along the route

parts.problem_md:
Coal production in the UK has declined in recent years. One reason given for this is that the social cost of coal production is too high.

What best describes the social cost of coal production?
parts.solution_md:
**D is correct** as the social cost equals the private cost plus the external costs

- A is incorrect as it does not account for external costs
- B is incorrect as the cost of travel is a private cost for the passengers when using the service
- C is incorrect as it does not account for any external costs

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: all the benefits of coal production minus all the costs of coal production

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: the cost of the environmental damage caused by coal production

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: the cost to the government of subsidising the coal industry

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: the private costs of coal production plus the external costs of coal production

parts.problem_md:
The government wants to reduce the consumption of cigarettes.

Which policy would be **most** likely to do this?
parts.solution_md:
**D is correct** as this raises the private costs to cigarette consumers which will reduce demand

- A is incorrect as it would have the opposite effect to the tax resulting in lower prices and greater demand
- B is incorrect as income tax is a broader tax and consumers may choose to spend less on healthy products and continue smoking
- C is incorrect as raising interest rates would have no effect on those who are not making loan repayments - and is some smokers are affected, they may choose to spend less on healthy products and continue smoking

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: increasing the indirect tax on cigarettes

parts.problem_md:
Sometimes the government regulates the market to protect the interests of consumers.

Which kind of regulation would achieve this protection?
parts.solution_md:
**B is correct** as preventing monopoly prices protects consumers from exploitation

- A is incorrect as by discouraging economies of scale, costs would increase leading to higher prices
- C is incorrect as shortening opening hours makes it more difficult for consumers to acquire goods/services
- D is incorrect as reducing the range of products works against the consumers ability to choose from a variety of goods/services

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: discouraging economies of scale that lead to lower costs

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: preventing mergers which result in high monopoly prices

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: reducing the range of products supplied to the market

parts.problem_md:
China has built a new railway in Kenya from the capital, Nairobi, to the seaport of Mombasa. Kenya must repay the cost of the railway to China. Journey time has been reduced significantly but fares have increased and farmers have lost agricultural land along the new line.

Who bears the external costs of this operation?
parts.solution_md:
**B is correct** as the external cost is the loss of farming land

- A is incorrect as China bears the private costs not the external costs
- C is incorrect as Keyna must repay the Chinese private cost
- D is incorrect as the cost of travel is a private cost for the passengers when using the service

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: China who built the new railway

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: farmers who have lost agricultural land

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: Kenya who must repay the cost to China

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: passengers who pay the higher fare

parts.problem_md:
In the diagram, which level of subsidy per kilo would a government have to give to producers to encourage them to increase production from 20 kilos per week to 30 kilos per week?

![nov-2018-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q18](assets/004-nov-2018-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q18.png)
parts.solution_md:
**C is correct** as the size of the required subsidy is the vertical distance between the two supply curves (\$20 - \$12)

- A is incorrect as \$3 is only a portion of the total distance between the two supply curves
- B is incorrect as \$5 is only a portion of the total distance between the two supply curves
- D is incorrect as \$15 is the new equilibrium price, not the size of the subsidy

parts.problem_md:
In a private market system certain goods and services would not be available unless the government intervened.

What does this identify in a private market?
parts.solution_md:
**C is correct** as the lack of goods in a market is considered to be market failure (e.g. merit goods like education)

- A is incorrect as market distribution refers to the flow of goods/services from the producer to the consumer
- B is incorrect as market equilibrium is where supply is equal to demand
- D is incorrect as market structure refers to the relationship that exists between buyers and sellers in a market

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows the equilibrium market price P<sub>E</sub> and quantity Q<sub>E</sub> for rice in a country.

![nov-2018-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q5](assets/005-nov-2018-v1qp-p1-cie-eco-q5.png)

Which government action could cause the market price for rice to become $P_{1}$?
parts.solution_md:
**A is correct **as an increase in exports will raise the price, leading to an increase in quantity supplied and a decrease in domestic quantity demanded

- B is incorrect as a maximum price below the market price would lower the price not increase it
- C is incorrect as a subsidy would lower the price, not increase it
- D is incorrect as the reduction of import tariffs will increase imports and lead to the domestic price to fall - not increase

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: encouraging the export of rice from the country

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: imposing a maximum price below the market price for rice

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: providing a subsidy to farmers to produce more rice

parts.problem_md: Which situation involving the building industry is most likely to be investigated by a government body set up to control restrictive practices?
parts.solution_md:
**B is correct** as price fixing is illegal as it results in higher prices and is unfair towards consumers

- A is incorrect as this is considered normal business activity not requiring government intervention
- C is incorrect as as this is considered normal competitive business activity not requiring government intervention
- D is incorrect as this is considered normal business activity not requiring government intervention

choices.label: A
choices.text_md: a builder purchasing a plot of land for development of housing

choices.label: B
choices.text_md: groups of suppliers of building materials agreeing to fix prices

choices.label: C
choices.text_md: several builders bidding for the same contracts

choices.label: D
choices.text_md: several builders using different sources of supply

parts.problem_md: What suggests that there is market failure?
parts.solution_md:
**C is correct **as a lack of competition leads to market failure

- A is incorrect as high producer profits can be a sign of a healthy market
- B is incorrect as high retail prices are normal for some products
- D is incorrect as the market may be functioning well with existing levels of investment
